anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: A memorial for generations until the age.
A statute for you and your sons.
Quoted: comparing spiritual things with spiritual.

choices.why: Origen's own word for the upward sense; keep it and gloss in the note.
With epistēmē: Moses arranges the rite as knowledge, not as bare story.

pass_a_gloss: And the witness by them is not lying in a prophetic voice only, but in the things done knowledge has been written, which the great prophet arranges knowledgeably for the race of the Hebrews, looking to the taking and keeping, and further also sacrificing and eating-by-fire and posture of clothing and haste toward the using-up of the thing sacredly-worked and the ashing of the things left and the lawful command being completed into their generations until an age as a memorial for them and their sons. For he confesses it to hold not only of history but also of [gap] anagogy, as it has been written: comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
pass_b_english: And the witness from them does not lie in a prophetic voice only. Knowledge has been written in the things that were done, which the great prophet arranges with knowledge for the race of the Hebrews, looking to the taking and the keeping, and further also the sacrificing and the eating by fire, and the posture of clothing, and the haste toward using up what has been sacredly offered, and the reducing to ash of what was left, and the lawful commandment being completed for their generations until the age as a memorial for them and for their sons. For he confesses that it holds not only of history but also of [lacuna] anagogy, as it is written: "Comparing spiritual things with spiritual." (Exodus 12:14) (1 Corinthians 2:13) (Exodus 12:24–27)
source_text: Ἔστι δὲ ἡ ὑπ’ α[ὐτ]ῶν μαρτυρία μὴ ἐν προ[φ]ητικῇ φωνῇ μόνῃ {ῳ} κει[μέν]ῃ, ἐν τοῖς πεπραγμένοις [δὲ γέγ]ραπται ἐπιστήμη, ἣν ἐ[πισ]τημονικῶς ὁ μέγας προφήτης διατάσσεται τῷ [γ]ένει τῶν Ἑβραίων, τήν τε λῆψιν κ[αὶ] τήρησιν {καὶ θυσίαν} ἐνορῶν ἔτι τε καὶ θύσιν καὶ βρῶσιν ἔμπυρον καὶ σχῆμα στολισμοῦ καὶ σπουδὴν πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ἱερουργηθέντος ἀνάλωσιν καὶ τὴν τῶν περιλειφθέντων τέφρωσιν καὶ τὴν ἔννομον ἐντολὴν εἰς γε[νεὰ]ς αὐτῶν μέχρις αἰῶνος [ἐκτε]λουμένην εἰς μνημ[όσυ]νον αὐτοῖς τε καὶ [το]ῖς υ[ἱοῖς] αὐτῶν· ὁμολογε[ῖ γὰ]ρ [οὐ μό]νον ἱστορία<ς> ἀλλὰ καὶ {π ...} ἀναγωγῆς ἔχεσθαι, κ[αθ]ὼς γέγραπται· "Πν(ευματ)ικὰ πν(ευματ)ικοῖς συγκρίνοντες".
